rules.title: AB 325 Cartwright Act: Common Pricing Algorithm Restrictions
rules.requirement: Under the Cartwright Act, it is unlawful to use or distribute common pricing algorithms as part of a conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce, or to coerce another person to set or adopt recommended prices or commercial terms.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies generally to persons using or distributing common pricing algorithms to restrain trade or coerce prices.

rules.exemptions: Does not include the end consumer of a product or service.
rules.citation: AB-325 / Business and Professions Code Section 16729
rules.quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
(b) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if the person coerces another person to set or adopt a recommended price or commercial term recommended by the common pricing algorithm for the same or similar products or services in the jurisdiction of this state.

rules.title: California Tenant Screening Fee Limits and Requirements
rules.requirement: The maximum tenant screening fee a landlord can charge a prospective tenant is capped at $68.96 for 2026, and landlords cannot charge a fee if no unit is available.

coverage_conditions.summary: Prospective tenants applying for residential rental units in California.

rules.quoted_span:
The maximum tenant screening fee for 2026 is
$68.96

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 - Just Cause for Termination
rules.requirement: Under the California Tenant Protection Act, landlords may not terminate a residential tenancy without just cause after 12 months of continuous occupancy (or 24 months if an adult tenant is added), requiring relocation assistance or a rent waiver for no-fault evictions.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to residential real property after 12 or 24 months of continuous occupancy, excluding hotels, institutional housing, certain owner-occupied properties, housing less than 15 years old, separately alienable properties under specific non-corporate ownership, and deed-restricted affordable housing.
coverage_conditions.owner_condition: Exempts certain single-family owner-occupied residences, owner-occupied duplexes, and non-corporate separately alienable properties meeting statutory ownership and notice requirements.
coverage_conditions.unresolvable: Tenancy duration and specific ownership corporate structures require facts beyond a simple address record.

rules.exemptions: Transient occupancy, nonprofit/religious/extended care/residential care facilities, dormitories, shared bathroom/kitchen with owner, certain single-family owner-occupied residences (including ADUs/JADUs or mobilehomes), owner-occupied two-unit structures, housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, certain separately alienable properties (not owned by a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member) with proper notice, and deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing.
rules.interaction: May preempt the listed local rules once in force; every affected address is flagged for human review rather than decided.
rules.quoted_span: Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
rules.conflict_note: possible preemption of r-0009 (Berkeley, CA), r-0014 (Los Angeles, CA), r-0018 (San Diego, CA), r-0021 (San Francisco, CA), r-0025 (Santa Ana, CA)

rules.title: Statewide Rent Increase Limits
rules.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from increasing gross rental rates by more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, over any 12-month period for applicable units.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to residential real property statewide, excluding government-subsidized housing, dormitories, housing subject to stricter local rent control, units issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, certain separately alienable properties without corporate/REIT ownership, and certain owner-occupied duplexes.
coverage_conditions.owner_condition: Exempts certain separately alienable properties (like single-family homes or condos) owned by individuals rather than corporations, REITs, or LLCs with corporate members, and owner-occupied duplexes.

rules.exemptions: Deed-restricted affordable housing, dormitories, stricter local rent control housing, units built within the last 15 years, certain independently alienable properties not owned by corporations/REITs/certain LLCs, and owner-occupied duplexes.
rules.interaction: Yields to stricter local law: where a listed local rule covers the unit, the local rule governs and this one is reported as superseded.
rules.quoted_span: Subject to subdivision (b), an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.

rules.title: Fair Employment and Housing Act Criminal History Restrictions
rules.requirement: Housing providers are prohibited from discriminating based on protected classes, source of income (such as Section 8 vouchers), and blanket criminal bans or arrest records without convictions, and must offer alternative credit evidence for subsidy holders.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to most housing accommodations and providers in California.
coverage_conditions.owner_condition: When an owner is occupying a home and is renting to one additional person, the owner may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics, though they still cannot make discriminatory advertisements.

rules.quoted_span: Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.

rules.title: Security Deposit Limit
rules.requirement: Landlords may generally only charge up to one month's rent as a security deposit (two months for qualifying small owners of two properties and four units max). Landlords must return deposits within 21 days with an itemized statement, photograph units before/after tenancy, and offer a move-out walk-through inspection.

coverage_conditions.summary: Most residential rental units, with exemptions for certain small landlords.
coverage_conditions.owner_condition: Exempts landlords who own no more than two rental properties with a total of no more than four residential units.

rules.exemptions: Landlords who own only two rental properties with no more than four residential units total if ownership is held by a natural person, family trust, or LLC where all members are natural persons.
rules.quoted_span: Starting July 1, 2024, many landlords may only charge one month's rent for unfurnished and furnished units

rules.title: Prohibition on Coordinated Pricing Algorithms
rules.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from using coordinated pricing algorithms to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential dwelling units, and vendors are prohibited from selling, licensing, or providing such algorithms to Berkeley landlords.

coverage_conditions.summary: All residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.

rules.exemptions: Excludes products that publish aggregated and anonymous rental data without recommending terms, products used to set rent/income limits under affordable housing guidelines, and data used strictly for financing research, appraisals, or software development and testing.
rules.quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described 
in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in 
the City of Berkeley.

rules.title: Prohibition of Non-Refundable Application Fees for Existing Tenancies
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot charge existing tenants a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy, or to add, replace, or remove a roommate. When charging a screening fee, landlords must also provide a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and state the maximum fee cap permitted under state law.

coverage_conditions.summary: All residential rental agreements in Berkeley.

rules.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.

rules.title: 2026 Relocation Assistance Payments for Owner Move-In and Ellis Act Evictions
rules.requirement: Landlords evicting tenants for an owner move-in or under the Ellis Act must pay a standard relocation assistance payment of $19,413, plus an additional $6,471 for qualifying households.

coverage_conditions.summary: Tenants subject to owner move-in evictions under the Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance or Ellis Act evictions under the Ellis Implementation Ordinance.
coverage_conditions.owner_condition: duplex was owner-occupied on December 31, 1979, and currently has an owner living in one of the units
coverage_conditions.unresolvable: Applicability determined by Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance and Ellis Implementation Ordinance coverage rules.

rules.citation: Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance; Ellis Implementation Ordinance
rules.quoted_span:
The standard relocation assistance payment will increase to
$19,413
.
The additional relocation assistance payment for qualifying households will increase to
$6,47
rules.conflict_note: may be preempted by r-0003 (California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 - Just Cause for Termination) from 2024-04-01

rules.title: Annual General Adjustment Maximum Cap
rules.requirement: The Annual General Adjustment (AGA) for fully covered rental units is capped at a maximum of 5% per year, regardless of higher Consumer Price Index calculation formulas.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to fully covered rental units under the Berkeley Rent Ordinance.

rules.quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%.

rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Under the Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance, landlords are prohibited from inquiring about, requiring disclosure of, or considering criminal history during advertising, application, tenant selection, or decision-making, and cannot charge higher rent or security deposits based on criminal history.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to rental housing providers in Berkeley, exempting owner-occupied properties with 1-3 units and specified limited exceptions.
coverage_conditions.owner_condition: Owner-occupied properties of 1 to 3 units where an owner of record resides in one unit as their primary residence.

rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8 properties; owner-occupied 1-3 unit properties; units under agreements allowing owner move-in under BMC 13.76.130 A.9; existing tenants seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates.
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.

rules.title: Security Deposit Interest
rules.requirement: Landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year, and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year, for tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance.

coverage_conditions.summary: Tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance.
coverage_conditions.owner_condition: Landlords who own only two rental properties with no more than four residential units total and ownership is held by a natural person, family trust, or LLC where all members are natural persons are exempt from the one-month limit.
coverage_conditions.unresolvable: Whether the unit is fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance

rules.exemptions: Units not covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance.
rules.quoted_span: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year.

rules.title: Instruction to Report on Algorithm-Based Rent Setting Ban
rules.requirement: The City Council instructed the Los Angeles Housing Department to report on entities using algorithm-based software to establish rents and the feasibility of a ban.

coverage_conditions.summary: Citywide rental housing

rules.quoted_span:
I THEREFORE MOVE that the City Council instruct the Los Angeles Housing Department to 
report on the number of ownership and management entities that are using algorithm-based 
software to establish rents and the feasibility of instituting a ban on the use of this software to set 
rents in the City.

rules.title: Just Cause For Eviction Ordinance
rules.requirement: Under the Just Cause For Eviction Ordinance, landlords are prohibited from terminating tenancies without just cause, must provide relocation assistance for no-fault evictions, and cannot evict for nonpayment unless rent owed exceeds the Fair Market Rent.

coverage_conditions.summary: Covers most residential properties in the City of Los Angeles not regulated by the City's Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) after the tenant has lived in the unit for at least six months or their original lease expired, whichever comes first.
coverage_conditions.owner_condition: Exemptions include owner's roommate and certain properties owned by HACLA or the government.
coverage_conditions.unresolvable: Tenant must have lived in the unit for at least six months or original lease expired; various specific exemptions apply including transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, owner's roommate, and certain non-profit or government facilities.

rules.exemptions: Transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, owner's roommate, cooperatives under certain circumstances, non-profit facilities for the homeless or short-term substance abuse treatment centers, and some properties owned by HACLA or the government.
rules.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.
rules.conflict_note: may be preempted by r-0003 (California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 - Just Cause for Termination) from 2024-04-01

rules.title: Annual Allowable Rent Increase for RSO Units (2025-2026)
rules.requirement: Annual rent increases for RSO units are limited to 3% from July 1, 2025, through June 30, 2026, and thereafter governed by a formula of 90% of the CPI change (min 1%, max 4%). Landlords can no longer include additional percentage increases for utilities as of February 2, 2026.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies generally to rental properties first built on or before October 1, 1978, as well as replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28, including apartments, condominiums and townhomes (if tenancy commenced on or before Dec 31, 1995), duplexes, two or more single-family units on a parcel, rooms in a hotel/motel/rooming house occupied for more than 30 consecutive days, residential units attached to a commercial building, ADUs, JADUs, and mobile homes.

rules.exemptions: Non-RSO properties are exempt from this specific limit and are subject to separate guidelines.
rules.quoted_span:
Annual rent increases for rental units subject to the City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO), effective
July 1, 2025, through June 30, 2026
is
3%

rules.title: Security Deposit Interest Requirement
rules.requirement: Landlords of properties subject to the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance must pay interest on security deposits to tenants either monthly or annually as a direct payment or rent credit after written notice.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to properties subject to the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (LARSO).
coverage_conditions.unresolvable: Properties subject to the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (LARSO)

rules.quoted_span: Interest shall begin accruing on November 1, 1990, on a monthly basis. A tenant shall be given the unpaid accrued interest in the form of either a direct payment or a credit against the tenant’s rent. The landlord shall choose between these two methods of payment and notify the tenant in writing of his or her choice.

rules.title: Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing
rules.requirement: It is unlawful for any person to sell, license, or provide an algorithmic device to a landlord, and for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to residential rental properties in the City of San Diego.

rules.exemptions: Does not include software used to publish reports from aggregated historical nonpublic competitor data older than 90 days or public information without recommending future rates/occupancy, software used to establish rates/income limits per affordable housing guidelines, or appraisal software that does not recommend rental rates during runtime operation.
rules.citation: San Diego Municipal Code ch. 9, art. 8, div. 11
rules.quoted_span:
It is unlawful for a person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an algorithmic
                            device to a landlord.

rules.title: Just Cause Required for Termination of Tenancy
rules.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from terminating a residential tenancy without just cause, categorized into at-fault and no-fault reasons, after tenancies lasting more than 30 days (with standard exemptions).

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to residential rental properties with specific exemptions such as recent construction (built within the last 15 years), transient occupancy, affordable housing units, and certain owner-occupied properties.
coverage_conditions.owner_condition: Exempts certain single-family homes and duplexes where the owner occupies a unit as their principal residence.

rules.exemptions: Transient/tourist hotels, short-term rentals, deed-restricted affordable housing, mobilehomes under Mobilehome Residency Law, hospitals/care facilities, university dorms, units sharing kitchen/bath with landlord, single-family homes with limited rooms/ADUs rented, owner-occupied duplexes, housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years, and certain separately alienable properties owned by natural persons.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this 
Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.
rules.conflict_note: may be preempted by r-0003 (California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 - Just Cause for Termination) from 2024-04-01

rules.title: Prohibition of Discrimination Based on a Tenant’s Source of Income
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot discriminate against tenants or applicants based on their source of income, including rental assistance from government, local, or nonprofit programs.

coverage_conditions.summary: All rental units in San Diego, except for owner-occupied units where the owner or family member shares a bathroom or kitchen with the tenant.
coverage_conditions.owner_condition: Owner or family member resides in the same building and shares a bathroom or kitchen facility with the tenant.

rules.exemptions: Tenancies in which the owner or any member of his or her family resides within the same residential building as the tenant and the owner or family member share a bathroom or a kitchen facility with the tenant or prospective tenant.
rules.quoted_span:
It is unlawful for any person to do any of the following acts, wholly or in
                           part, based on a person’s source of income (except as may be necessary to
                           comply with any program requirements related to source of income):

                           1.     To refuse to enter into or renew an agreement for tenancy;

                           2.     To interrupt or terminate any tenancy;

                           3.     To falsely represent that a rental-unit is not available for tenancy;

                           4.     To require inclusion in the terms of an agreement for tenancy any
                                  clause, condition, or restriction; or

                           5.     To restrict a tenant’s access to facilities or services on real property
                                  associated with the tenancy, or refuse repairs or improvements to real
                                  property associated with the tenancy.

rules.title: Prohibition of Algorithmic Devices for Rent Setting
rules.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from using software or algorithmic devices that analyze nonpublic competitor rental data to recommend rental prices or manage occupancy levels for residential units.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to residential units in San Francisco.

rules.quoted_span: The law prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco.

rules.title: Just Cause Requirement for Evictions
rules.requirement: Landlords must have one of 17 permitted just cause reasons to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance.

coverage_conditions.summary: Covers rental units covered by the Rent Ordinance, including some units exempt from rent increases such as post-June 13, 1979 construction and Costa-Hawkins eligible units.

rules.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction.
rules.conflict_note: may be preempted by r-0003 (California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 - Just Cause for Termination) from 2024-04-01

rules.title: Annual Allowable Rent Increase for 2026-2027
rules.requirement: The annual allowable rent increase for rent-controlled units is set to 1.6% from March 1, 2026, through February 28, 2027.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to rent-controlled units in San Francisco.

rules.quoted_span: For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable increase amount effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6%.

rules.title: Security Deposit Interest Rate
rules.requirement: Landlords must pay interest on security deposits at the rate of 4.2% for the period from March 1, 2026, to February 28, 2027.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to residential security deposits held under city rules.

rules.citation: San Francisco Rent Board Current Rates
rules.quoted_span: 4.2% for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027

rules.title: Ban on Algorithmic Rent Pricing Software
rules.requirement: Landlords and apartment owners are prohibited from using automated AI software or algorithmic rent-setting devices relying on nonpublic competitor data to set rental prices, subject to civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to residential rental property within Santa Ana city limits, excluding pricing software using solely publicly available data, aggregate historical data, or tools for affordable housing program compliance.

rules.quoted_span: To protect renters, city leaders have approved a new ordinance that stops apartment owners and landlords from using automated AI software to set rental prices.

rules.title: Just Cause for Eviction and Relocation Assistance
rules.requirement: Landlords must have a valid just cause reason to evict a tenant and must provide relocation assistance (such as 3 months of relocation assistance or waived rent) for no-fault evictions.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to residential properties after 30 days, with specific exclusions such as housing produced in the last 15 years and deed-restricted affordable housing.

rules.citation: Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Your landlord must have a valid reason to evict you. This could be for not paying rent, breaking the lease, or if the landlord wants to move into the property themselves.
rules.conflict_note: may be preempted by r-0003 (California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 - Just Cause for Termination) from 2024-04-01

rules.title: Maximum Rent Increase Limit
rules.requirement: Annual rent increases are capped at the lower of 3% of the current rent or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change over the most recent 12-month period.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to residential buildings, excluding those constructed after February 1, 1995, and mobile home spaces offered after January 1, 1990.

rules.citation: Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: The increase cannot be more than 3% of your current rent or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change, whichever is less.

rules.title: Tenant Fee Responsibility for Real Estate Brokers and Salespersons
rules.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from charging prospective tenants application fees or upfront charges besides authorized move-in amounts, and broker fees must be paid exclusively by the party who originally engaged the broker.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to lessors/landlords statewide.

rules.quoted_span: Any fee shall only be paid by the party, lessor or tenant who originally engaged and entered into a contract with the licensed broker or salesperson.

rules.title: Notice to determine estate at will and cure for nonpayment
rules.requirement: For tenancies at will, a landlord must provide a 14-day written notice to quit for nonpayment of rent with a 10-day cure period, and reprisals against tenants for reporting violations are prohibited.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to estates at will.

rules.quoted_span: In case of neglect or refusal to pay the rent due from a tenant at will, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the tenancy; provided, that the tenancy of a tenant who has not received a similar notice from the landlord within the twelve months next preceding the receipt of such notice shall not be determined if the tenant, within ten days after the receipt thereof, pays or tenders to the landlord, the landlord's attorney, or the person to whom the tenant customarily pays rent, the full amount of any rent due.

rules.title: General prohibition on rent control with voluntary exception
rules.requirement: Cities and towns are generally prohibited from enacting or enforcing rent control, except that municipalities accepting the chapter may adopt a voluntary rent control system.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to rental units unless owned by a person or entity owning less than ten units or having a fair market rent exceeding $400.
coverage_conditions.owner_condition: Exempts units owned by a person or entity owning less than ten rental units.

rules.exemptions: Rental units owned by a person or entity owning less than ten rental units or having a fair market rent exceeding $400.

No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except that any city or town that accepts this chapter may adopt rent control regulation that provides:

rules.title: Initiative Petition 25-21 to Limit Rent Increases
rules.requirement: Proposed statewide rent control ballot measures that would have capped annual rent increases at the lesser of CPI or 5% were struck down by the Supreme Judicial Court.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to most residential rental units, with exemptions for owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units, newly constructed units less than 10 years old, certain publicly regulated units, short-term rentals, and educational, religious, or nonprofit facilities.

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units, newly constructed units less than 10 years old, certain publicly regulated units, short-term rentals, and dwelling units in facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or nonprofit purposes.
rules.citation: Initiative Petition 25-21 / Cella v. Attorney General, SJC-13893
rules.quoted_span: Under the proposed law, annual rent increases would have been limited to the lesser of the annual increase in the Consumer Price Index or 5%. The petition included several exemptions, including owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units, newly constructed units less than 10 years old, certain publicly regulated units, short-term rentals, and dwelling units in facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or nonprofit purposes.

rules.title: Housing accommodations discrimination in rental or sale
rules.requirement: It is unlawful for housing owners, lessors, brokers, or managing agents to discriminate in terms, conditions, or privileges based on protected classes, including public assistance, children, and handicap.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to publicly assisted, multiple dwelling, or contiguously located housing accommodations, condominiums, and housing cooperatives.
coverage_conditions.owner_condition: Exempts dwellings of 3 apartments or less where one is occupied by an elderly/infirm person for whom children would be a hardship, temporary leasing of a principal residence up to one year, or a single unit in a two-family dwelling owner-occupied.

rules.exemptions: Age restrictions do not apply to minors, elderly housing developments, or certain 55+ or 62+ communities complying with federal law.
rules.quoted_span: For the owner, lessee, sublessee, licensed real estate broker, assignee or managing agent of publicly assisted or multiple dwelling or contiguously located housing accommodations or other person having the right of ownership or possession or right to rent or lease, or sell or negotiate for the sale of such accommodations, or any agent or employee of such a person, or any organization of unit owners in a condominium or housing cooperative: (a) to refuse to rent or lease or sell or negotiate for sale or otherwise to deny to or withhold from any person or group of persons such accommodations because of the race, religious creed, color, national origin, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, which shall not include persons whose sexual orientation involves minor children as the sex object, age, genetic information, ancestry, or marital status of such person or persons or because such person is a veteran or member of the armed forces, or because such person is blind, or hearing impaired or has any other handicap

rules.requirement: Landlords may not require move-in amounts exceeding first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit equal to one month's rent, and lock costs, and must return security deposits within 30 days after termination of occupancy.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to residential real property tenancies excluding vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less.

rules.exemptions: Leases, rentals, occupancy or tenancies of 100 days or less in duration for vacation or recreational purposes.

rules.requirement: The city council passed a policy order to initiate steps toward banning residential property management companies from using algorithmic and AI-driven models to recommend rent prices.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to residential property management companies using algorithmic pricing models.

rules.quoted_span: City council also unanimously passed a policy order initiating steps to ban residential property management companies from contracting companies that use algorithmic and AI-driven models to recommend what they should charge for rent.

rules.title: Source of Income Discrimination Prohibition
rules.requirement: Landlords, sellers, and rental agents are prohibited from discriminating against applicants based on their source of income, explicitly including Section 8 and public benefits.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to housing in Cambridge, with an exemption for owner-occupied 2-family dwellings.
coverage_conditions.owner_condition: Exempts 2-family dwellings when the owner lives there.

rules.exemptions: 2-family dwellings when the owner lives there
rules.quoted_span: Source of Income, includes Section 8 and public benefits

rules.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
rules.requirement: The Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act makes it unlawful for a rental property owner or coordinator to use algorithmic software that collects competitors' nonpublic leasing information to set or recommend rental prices, lease terms, or occupancy levels.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to residential rental dwelling units statewide, excluding inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, and detention or correctional facilities.

rules.exemptions: Does not apply to conducting research or statistical analysis without setting terms, providing publicly available estimated rent amounts, using real estate brokerage databases available on equal terms that do not set prices or collect sensitive info, or government entities setting rents through affordability controls.
rules.interaction: May preempt the listed local rules once in force; every affected address is flagged for human review rather than decided.
rules.quoted_span:
It
shall be unlawful and a violation of the “New Jersey Antitrust Act,” P.L.1970,
c.73 (C.56:9-1 et seq.) for:
a.     a rental property owner, or any agent,
representative, or subcontractor thereof, to receive, subscribe to, contract
for, or otherwise exchange any form of consideration in return for the use of,
the services of a coordinator;
b.    a coordinator to facilitate a tacit or express
agreement among rental property owners that restricts competition with respect
to residential dwelling units, including by performing a coordinating
function;

rules.title: Application Fee Cap
rules.requirement: Landlords and their agents cannot charge a residential rental application or screening fee exceeding $50, subject to annual adjustments based on the Consumer Price Index.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to residential rental properties, excluding one-family or two-family dwellings offered for rent and real estate licensees acting as agents rather than landlords.

rules.exemptions: One-family or two-family dwellings offered for rent; a licensee of the New Jersey Real Estate Commission unless the licensee is the landlord.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord, or
agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply
to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which
exceeds $50.

rules.title: New Jersey Anti-Eviction Act Good Cause Requirement
rules.requirement: Landlords may not remove residential tenants or fail to renew leases except for specific statutory grounds of good cause. Displaced tenants due to illegal occupancy are entitled to relocation assistance equal to six times the monthly rent if the municipality has no ordinance.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to residential properties generally, with explicit exclusions for certain owner-occupied premises, hotels/motels, and specific family trusts or units occupied by immediate family members with developmental disabilities.
coverage_conditions.owner_condition: Exempts owner-occupied premises with not more than two rental units, or certain immediate family occupancy arrangements.

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises with not more than two rental units, hotels, motels, seasonal or transient guests, and certain immediate family member occupancies.
rules.quoted_span:
No lessee or tenant or the assigns, under-tenants or legal representatives of such lessee or tenant may be
      removed by the Superior Court from any house, building, mobile home or land in a mobile home park or
      tenement leased for residential purposes, other than (1) owner-occupied premises with not more than two
      rental units or a hotel, motel or other guest house or part thereof rented to a transient guest or seasonal
      tenant; (2) a dwelling unit which is held in trust on behalf of a member of the immediate family of the person
      or persons establishing the trust, provided that the member of the immediate family on whose behalf the
      trust is established permanently occupies the unit; and (3) a dwelling unit which is permanently occupied by
      a member of the immediate family of the owner of that unit, provided, however, that exception (2) or (3)
      shall apply only in cases in which the member of the immediate family has a developmental disability,
      except upon establishment of one of the following grounds as good cause:

rules.title: Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Rent Control Exemption
rules.requirement: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from local rent control ordinances for a period of 30 years following completion of construction.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to newly constructed multiple dwellings.

rules.interaction: May preempt the listed local rules once in force; every affected address is flagged for human review rather than decided.
rules.quoted_span:
Under the Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Law ( N.J.S.A. 2A:42 -84.5), newly 
constructed multiple dwellings shall be exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period 
of 30 years following completion of construction of the building.
rules.conflict_note: possible preemption of r-0047 (Hoboken, NJ), r-0049 (Jersey City, NJ), r-0050 (Newark, NJ)

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - Criminal Record Screening Limitations
rules.requirement: Housing providers are prohibited from inquiring about an applicant's criminal record prior to issuing a conditional offer of rental housing, and are prohibited from discriminating in housing based on protected classes including race, religion, color, national origin, sex, disability, and source of lawful income.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to rental dwelling units in New Jersey, excluding dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
coverage_conditions.owner_condition: owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are exempt

rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
rules.quoted_span:
A
housing provider
shall not require an applicant to
complete any housing application that includes any inquiries regarding an
applicant’s criminal record prior to the provision of a conditional offer,
except that a housing provider may consider whether an applicant has ever been
convicted of drug-related criminal activity for the manufacture or production
of methamphetamine on the premises of federally assisted housing, and whether
the applicant is subject to a lifetime registration requirement under a State
sex offender registration program.

rules.title: Maximum Security Deposit Limit
rules.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from charging a security deposit exceeding one and one-half times one month's rent, and must deposit funds in an interest-bearing account, returning the deposit plus interest within 30 days of lease termination.

coverage_conditions.summary: All rental premises or units used for dwelling purposes, except owner-occupied premises with not more than two rental units where the tenant has not provided 30 days written notice.
coverage_conditions.owner_condition: owner-occupied premises with not more than two rental units
coverage_conditions.unresolvable: tenant must provide 30 days written notice for owner-occupied premises with <= 2 units

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings
rules.quoted_span:
The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than 
one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ).

rules.title: City of Hoboken outlaws algorithmic rent-fixing
rules.requirement: Landlords renting residential units in Hoboken are prohibited from using software, algorithms, or data-sharing platforms to coordinate, recommend, or implement rental prices, lease terms, or occupancy levels among competing landlords.

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential units in Hoboken

rules.citation: City of Hoboken legislation adopted July 9, 2025
rules.quoted_span: It will now be illegal for landlords renting residential units in Hoboken to engage in price-fixing through algorithmic rent-fixing, meaning they can no longer use software, algorithms, or data-sharing platforms to coordinate, recommend, or implement rental prices, lease terms, or occupancy levels among competing landlords.
rules.conflict_note: may be preempted by r-0040 (Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act) from 2027-07-01

rules.title: Hoboken Rent Leveling Increase Cap
rules.requirement: No landlord may request or receive a percentage increase in rent which is greater than 5% under the city rent leveling ordinance.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to residential rental units under the city's rent leveling regulations.

rules.quoted_span:
No landlord may request or
                                                                                                       receive a percentage increase in
                                                                                                       rent which is greater than 5%
rules.conflict_note: may be preempted by r-0043 (Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Rent Control Exemption) from None

rules.title: Jersey City Code § 218-12
rules.requirement: Landlords in Jersey City Code § 218-12 are prohibited from using algorithmic rent coordination services.

coverage_conditions.summary: Multifamily housing landlords

rules.quoted_span: Prohibits a landlord’s use of algorithmic rent coordination services
rules.conflict_note: may be preempted by r-0040 (Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act) from 2027-07-01

rules.title: Jersey City Rent Control Exemption for 1-4 Unit Properties
rules.requirement: All 1 to 4 unit properties are exempt from Jersey City's rent control regulations.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to properties with 1 to 4 units.

rules.exemptions: Properties with 1 to 4 units are exempt.
rules.citation: Chapter 260 of the Jersey City Municipal Code
rules.quoted_span: All 1-4 Unit Properties are exempt from rent control
rules.conflict_note: may be preempted by r-0043 (Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Rent Control Exemption) from None

rules.title: Annual CPI-U Based Rent Increase Limit
rules.requirement: Landlords may increase rent annually based on the applicable monthly Consumer Price Index-Urban (CPI-U) percentage published for the relevant month, provided they give proper written notice.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to residential dwellings in Newark except public housing, hotels, motels, commercial spaces, and explicitly exempted new constructions or substantially rehabilitated units.

rules.exemptions: Public housing, motel or hotel space rented day-to-day, commercial use, newly constructed multiple dwellings with a 30-year exemption certificate, and substantially rehabilitated dwellings meeting specific criteria.
rules.quoted_span:
Beginning June 20, 2014
         permissible annual rent increases for a given month are shown in the table below. Landlords may
         increase rents as per the Consumer Price Index- Urban percentage (CPI-U %) published every
         month.
rules.conflict_note: may be preempted by r-0043 (Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Rent Control Exemption) from None
